## Solutions to Simplify Your Business

Discover our innovative technology and services designed to simplify operations, reduce costs, and
maximize your efficiency.

## Simplify Your Ordering Process

Order online anytime, track deliveries, and manage your inventory with ease using Gordon Ordering.

[Learn More >][25]

## On The Go With Our App

The Gordon Now App lets you place orders, browse products, and manage your account right from your
mobile device.

[Learn More >][26]

## Optimize Your Menu Management

Gordon Restaurant Pro helps you control costs, plan menus, and analyze sales data to maximize
profitability.

[Learn More >][27]

## Find the Right Tech for Your Restaurant

Navigate hundreds of tech options to discover the best fit for your operations—plus, access to
exclusive deals.

[Explore All Solutions >][28]

## Delivering Quality & Expertise

Explore our wide range of products and services designed to enhance your operations and delight your
customers.

## Quality Ingredients, Delivered On Time

We offer a wide selection of fresh, frozen, and dry goods to meet all your menu needs.

[**Explore Products**][29]

## Reliable Distribution Network

Our established distribution network ensures your orders are delivered on time and ready for
application.

[**Learn More**][30]

## Trusted Brands, Exceptional Value

Discover our exclusive brands that help you cut costs without sacrificing quality.

[**View Our Brands**][31]

## Specialized Solutions for Your Needs

Our specialty companies provide tailored solutions for specific foodservice tastes and operational
needs.

[**Learn More**][32]

## Essential Equipment & Supplies

Find a comprehensive selection of kitchen equipment, tabletop items, and supplies.

[**Browse Supplies**][33]

## Innovative Technology Solutions

Streamline your operations with our user-friendly online ordering, inventory management, and menu
planning tools.

[**Explore Technology**][34]

## Culinary Expertise & Support

Access culinary resources, trends, and expert advice to inspire your menu and enhance your
offerings.

[**Explore Support**][35]

## Committed to Sustainability

We offer sustainable products and practices to help you reduce your environmental impact.

[**Learn About Sustainability**][36]

## A Legacy of Excellence

With over 125 years of experience, Gordon Food Service is a trusted partner for foodservice
businesses across North America.

CAREERS

## Start Your Future
## With Us Today

Whether you are looking to work with your hands in operations, jump behind the scenes in the Home
Office, or serve our customers directly in transportation and sales, we have a place for you! We
welcome individuals with unique perspectives and talents. With a variety of positions available,
explore our careers and apply today if you find a role that fits your passion!

[ Explore Careers ][37]
[ See Open Positions ][38]

We provide valuable resources to help you adapt, innovate, and thrive in the ever-evolving

[ Become a Customer ][39]

Stay informed about upcoming food shows and events to network and discover new products.

[Read the Insights >][42]

Find innovative recipes, menu ideas, and culinary inspiration to delight your customers.

[Get Inspired >][43]

Improve efficiency, manage costs, and enhance your business strategy with expert guidance.

[Learn More >][44]

See how we have helped foodservice businesses thrive through partnership and tailored solutions.

## DELIVERIES

**Convenient. Dependable. Trackable.**

We're committed to making it easier for customers to get what they need, when they need it, with
greater flexibility and more responsive service through a range of delivery options.

Quality products delivered with consistency.

An unmatched portfolio of quality products that consistently deliver on expectations.

## MORE
## TOOLS

From MOXē® to full suites of digital solutions such as CHECK® Business Tools and VITALS, we can help
you run your business with ease.

inventory management.

resources–
allowing you to maximize coverage and enable flexibility as you grow.

their brand and bring in more diners. Find out more.

comes next. US Foods® helps you adapt with confidence and keep your menu fired up.

# Hand-Rolled Sourdough Pretzels

## Taste the difference of a hand-rolled pretzel.

Making sourdough pretzels the old fashioned way since 1931, our family recipe dates back to the late
1800s. Why does this matter? We allow our yeast to achieve its full rising potential before
hand-rolling, twisting, and salting each pretzel. Our pretzel making process and family recipe
create a flavor, texture, and sourdough quality that cannot be duplicated by mass-produced,
machine-stamped pretzels.

Our [online shop][27] offers handmade sourdough pretzels that come in unsalted, lightly salted,
regular, salty, extra-salty, and dark-salted pretzels. Add on our zesty dipping mustard, a Hammond’s
classic t-shirt, or subscribe for a monthly discount. Visit [Hammond’s Pretzel Bakery Store][28] in
Lancaster, PA, in person to purchase our hand-rolled sourdough pretzels, where you, family, and
friends can see and smell our pretzels being made on site. Or shop at the hundreds of retailers in
Lancaster, York, Lebanon and beyond.

### Buy sourdough pretzels online.

We make a variety of pretzels, from unsalted to extra-salty. Explore our different-sized packaging:
bags, snack packs, boxes, and bulk boxes. Shop Hammond’s classic or seasonal cans.

Get pretzels for everyday, game day, office snacks, and events.

# Hand-Rolled Sourdough Pretzels

## Taste the difference of a hand-rolled pretzel.

Making sourdough pretzels the old fashioned way since 1931, our family recipe dates back to the late
1800s. Why does this matter? We allow our yeast to achieve its full rising potential before
hand-rolling, twisting, and salting each pretzel. Our pretzel making process and family recipe
create a flavor, texture, and sourdough quality that cannot be duplicated by mass-produced,
machine-stamped pretzels.

Our [online shop][27] offers handmade sourdough pretzels that come in unsalted, lightly salted,
regular, salty, extra-salty, and dark-salted pretzels. Add on our zesty dipping mustard, a Hammond’s
classic t-shirt, or subscribe for a monthly discount. Visit [Hammond’s Pretzel Bakery Store][28] in
Lancaster, PA, in person to purchase our hand-rolled sourdough pretzels, where you, family, and
friends can see and smell our pretzels being made on site. Or shop at the hundreds of retailers in
Lancaster, York, Lebanon and beyond.

### Buy sourdough pretzels online.

We make a variety of pretzels, from unsalted to extra-salty. Explore our different-sized packaging:
bags, snack packs, boxes, and bulk boxes. Shop Hammond’s classic or seasonal cans.

Get pretzels for everyday, game day, office snacks, and events.

[[Sake Expert logo]][11]

distribute. Whether you’re a connoisseur or just starting your journey into sake, we invite you to
check our extensive list. Discover unique flavors, learn more about your favorite drinks, and
elevate your drinking experience through JFC’s Sake Expert.

## Answers before you ask.

Why choose Macar & Sons?

We've been a premier Mediterranean food import and distribution company since 1995. Because we
import directly instead of reselling, you get better pricing, fresher rotation, and the products
your customers actually ask for — delivered faster.

Do you sell to businesses like mine?

Yes — we supply grocery stores, restaurants, hotels, caterers and food service businesses of every
size, from single-location bistros to large retail chains, with order sizes tailored to your needs.

Are your products Halal?

We carry a wide range of 100% Halal certified products that have passed strict controls from
reputable certifying organizations.

How fast is delivery, and where do you ship?

We deliver nationwide to all 50 states, with orders typically arriving in 1–3 business days from our
tri-temperature warehouse in Pompano Beach, Florida.

Can I see pricing before I order?

Yes — our order portal shows live pricing and real-time product availability, with automated volume
discounts applied as you build your order.

Hi, we’re Eric and Lisa! Welcome, we’re so glad that you’re here! Recipes from Europe celebrates
food, family, and culture.

It’s about reconnecting with old recipes that were family favorites, learning about a country’s
cuisine, and getting inspired to taste something new. 

Together with our European contributors, we share recipes from across Europe to help you explore
this part of the world.

### About Snyder’s of Hanover

At Snyder’s of Hanover, we’re all about crafting mouthwatering snacks that bring joy to your taste
buds. With a rich heritage rooted in tradition, we’ve been satisfying snack cravings since 1909.

Our journey began with a simple passion for pretzels, and today, we proudly stand as leaders in the
pretzel industry and a beloved name in the world of snacks. Each bite of our products reflects our
commitment to quality ingredients and delicious flavors.

From classic pretzels in all shapes and sizes to pretzel pieces coated with bursts of flavor, we
offer something for every palate and occasion. Whether you’re enjoying a movie night at home or need
a tasty treat on the go, Snyder’s of Hanover has you covered.

### 1909

Harry Warehime began producing Olde Tyme Pretzels.

### 1920s

In the early 1920s, Grandma Eda and Edward Snyder II began frying potato chips in a kettle at their
summer home, and they sold the snacks door-to-door, at fairs and farmer’s markets. Meanwhile, their
son William V. and his wife Helen were making angel food cakes for local stores.

### 1924

The family united forces as Snyder’s Bakery, where they made everything from angel food cakes to
fresh noodles until the automated snack production process took over.

### 1940

Modernization was underway in the 1940s with a new plant built on Lafayette and Granger Streets
including an automated direct fire ferry fryer. William Snyder, E. Wise and H. Ness joined together
to create the Potato Chip Institute to improve communication among competing “chippers”.

Snyder’s grew distribution south to Norfolk, VA, west to Pittsburgh, PA and north to New York as the
company began using aluminum foil bags to extend the shelf life of products in these distant markets
– it was a first for the industry, and a very practical innovation. A new plant in Berlin, PA was
built to handle growing demand.


### 1950

In 1950, the Berlin plant was sold to William’s sister and her husband, Edith and Clair “Barb”
Sterner. Eleven years later, William’s son, William “Billy” L. Snyder, sold the Hanover plant to
Hanover Canning, headed by Alan R. Warehime.


### 1961

By the early 1960s, sales had reached about $400,000.

### 1963

The Bechtel Pretzel Company, founded in 1947 by Bill and Helen Bechtel, was purchased and
incorporated into Snyder’s Bakery. Bill developed the original recipe for the Sourdough Hard Pretzel
that is still enjoyed by consumers today.

### 1966

Michael Warehime, Alan’s youngest son, joined the company. He was named President and Chief
Executive Officer in 1972 and Chairman of the Board in 1990. Our growth, new product development,
and strong emphasis on quality in all that we do are attributed to Mike and his vision and
leadership.

### 1980

Nineteen years after Snyder’s was purchased, the Warehime family decided to “spin off” the Snyder’s
of Hanover^{®} Snack Operation from Hanover Brands, enabling the companies to focus on their
respective industries of snacks and vegetables. Snyder’s sales in 1980 were $15.8 million. After the
split, both companies exploded, growing faster than industry averages.

### 1984

California-style corn tortilla chips were added to Snyder’s snack line.

### 1989

On Saturday, December 2, 1989, our flagship Hanover pretzel bakery burned to the ground when an
overhead heater malfunctioned and fire started in the warehouse area. Fire departments from many
surrounding communities fought the dramatic and overwhelming blaze. The “glow” could be seen in the
night sky for miles around. It smoldered for several days. Fortunately, no one was injured. Pretzel
production continued at the Granger Street facility. Our employees pulled together and completed a
massive cleanup and the building was rebuilt and expanded regularly. Today, it is over 400,000
square feet and includes product processing, packaging, and warehousing as well as a large research
and development laboratory.

### 1992

Flavored pretzel pieces burst onto the market with Honey Mustard & Onion flavor, with Buttermilk
Ranch and Cheddar Cheese following the year after.

Our Olde Tyme Pretzels, first made in 1909 by H.V. Warehime, took the Automatic Merchandiser’s

In September 2013 Snyder’s of Hanover^{®} introduced two new Certified Gluten-Free Pretzel Sticks

Sweet and Salty Pretzel Pieces and Pretzel Spoonz are introduced.

### 2015

In February 2015, Snyder’s of Hanover introduced Pretzel Poppers in 3 flavors.

### 2016

Snyder’s of Hanover introduces Peanut Butter Filled Pieces and S’mores flavored Pretzel Pieces.

### About Snyder’s of Hanover

At Snyder’s of Hanover, we’re all about crafting mouthwatering snacks that bring joy to your taste
buds. With a rich heritage rooted in tradition, we’ve been satisfying snack cravings since 1909.

Our journey began with a simple passion for pretzels, and today, we proudly stand as leaders in the
pretzel industry and a beloved name in the world of snacks. Each bite of our products reflects our
commitment to quality ingredients and delicious flavors.

From classic pretzels in all shapes and sizes to pretzel pieces coated with bursts of flavor, we
offer something for every palate and occasion. Whether you’re enjoying a movie night at home or need
a tasty treat on the go, Snyder’s of Hanover has you covered.

### 1909

Harry Warehime began producing Olde Tyme Pretzels.

### 1920s

In the early 1920s, Grandma Eda and Edward Snyder II began frying potato chips in a kettle at their
summer home, and they sold the snacks door-to-door, at fairs and farmer’s markets. Meanwhile, their
son William V. and his wife Helen were making angel food cakes for local stores.

### 1924

The family united forces as Snyder’s Bakery, where they made everything from angel food cakes to
fresh noodles until the automated snack production process took over.

### 1940

Modernization was underway in the 1940s with a new plant built on Lafayette and Granger Streets
including an automated direct fire ferry fryer. William Snyder, E. Wise and H. Ness joined together
to create the Potato Chip Institute to improve communication among competing “chippers”.

Snyder’s grew distribution south to Norfolk, VA, west to Pittsburgh, PA and north to New York as the
company began using aluminum foil bags to extend the shelf life of products in these distant markets
– it was a first for the industry, and a very practical innovation. A new plant in Berlin, PA was
built to handle growing demand.


### 1950

In 1950, the Berlin plant was sold to William’s sister and her husband, Edith and Clair “Barb”
Sterner. Eleven years later, William’s son, William “Billy” L. Snyder, sold the Hanover plant to
Hanover Canning, headed by Alan R. Warehime.


### 1961

By the early 1960s, sales had reached about $400,000.

### 1963

The Bechtel Pretzel Company, founded in 1947 by Bill and Helen Bechtel, was purchased and
incorporated into Snyder’s Bakery. Bill developed the original recipe for the Sourdough Hard Pretzel
that is still enjoyed by consumers today.

### 1966

Michael Warehime, Alan’s youngest son, joined the company. He was named President and Chief
Executive Officer in 1972 and Chairman of the Board in 1990. Our growth, new product development,
and strong emphasis on quality in all that we do are attributed to Mike and his vision and
leadership.

### 1980

Nineteen years after Snyder’s was purchased, the Warehime family decided to “spin off” the Snyder’s
of Hanover^{®} Snack Operation from Hanover Brands, enabling the companies to focus on their
respective industries of snacks and vegetables. Snyder’s sales in 1980 were $15.8 million. After the
split, both companies exploded, growing faster than industry averages.

### 1984

California-style corn tortilla chips were added to Snyder’s snack line.

### 1989

On Saturday, December 2, 1989, our flagship Hanover pretzel bakery burned to the ground when an
overhead heater malfunctioned and fire started in the warehouse area. Fire departments from many
surrounding communities fought the dramatic and overwhelming blaze. The “glow” could be seen in the
night sky for miles around. It smoldered for several days. Fortunately, no one was injured. Pretzel
production continued at the Granger Street facility. Our employees pulled together and completed a
massive cleanup and the building was rebuilt and expanded regularly. Today, it is over 400,000
square feet and includes product processing, packaging, and warehousing as well as a large research
and development laboratory.

### 1992

Flavored pretzel pieces burst onto the market with Honey Mustard & Onion flavor, with Buttermilk
Ranch and Cheddar Cheese following the year after.

Our Olde Tyme Pretzels, first made in 1909 by H.V. Warehime, took the Automatic Merchandiser’s

In 2011 Snyder’s of Hanover^{®} built a 26-Acre Solar field- the largest in Pennsylvania. It has

Flavors: Hot Buffalo Wing and Honey, Mustard & Onion.

Sweet and Salty Pretzel Pieces and Pretzel Spoonz are introduced.

### 2015

In February 2015, Snyder’s of Hanover introduced Pretzel Poppers in 3 flavors.

Snyder’s of Hanover introduces Peanut Butter Filled Pieces and S’mores flavored Pretzel Pieces.

The Challenge

## The agri-food industry runs on opacity and manual effort.

01

### Information Asymmetry

Buyers and suppliers operate with wildly different levels of market visibility. Pricing,
availability, and quality data are fragmented, outdated, or locked behind intermediaries.

02

### Trust & Verification Gap

Finding reliable counterparties requires years of relationship-building, trade shows, and manual due
diligence. Verification is slow, expensive, and often unreliable.

03

### Execution Bottleneck

Even when opportunities are identified, execution remains manual -- outreach, negotiation, logistics
coordination, compliance, and follow-ups consume enormous time and resources.

OUR VISION

## Agri-food trade should work for everyone in it.

We believe that transparent data, verified networks, and intelligent automation can eliminate the
friction that holds global food trade back. Every buyer deserves fair prices. Every supplier
deserves market access. Every transaction should be efficient.

Data LayerNetwork LayerAI Layer

Together, these three layers form the foundation for a fundamentally better way to trade food
globally.

## The agri-food industry runs on opacity and manual effort.

01

### Information Asymmetry

Buyers and suppliers operate with wildly different levels of market visibility. Pricing,
availability, and quality data are fragmented, outdated, or locked behind intermediaries.

02

### Trust & Verification Gap

Finding reliable counterparties requires years of relationship-building, trade shows, and manual due
diligence. Verification is slow, expensive, and often unreliable.

03

### Execution Bottleneck

Even when opportunities are identified, execution remains manual -- outreach, negotiation, logistics
coordination, compliance, and follow-ups consume enormous time and resources.

OUR VISION

## Agri-food trade should work for everyone in it.

We believe that transparent data, verified networks, and intelligent automation can eliminate the
friction that holds global food trade back. Every buyer deserves fair prices. Every supplier
deserves market access. Every transaction should be efficient.

globally.
